name: Street Safety and Attractiveness in Frankfurt
description:
Method replication: participants imagine walking through 20 street-level views of Frankfurt am Main, rate how safe each place feels and how attractive it looks on 5-point scales, and at the end explain in their own words what made streets feel safe or attractive; the images are not the paper's stimuli (124 Google Street View images, 2022–2023, taken at locations sampled from the authors' open dataset of 753 rated points).

Original study: Milias, Sharifi Noorian, Bozzon & Psyllidis (2023), AGILE GIScience Series 4, 8. With a crowdsourcing tool, 403 participants virtually navigated city streets in Frankfurt through sequences of street-level images, rated locations on perceived safety and attractiveness (5-point Likert) and explained their ratings in their own words, giving 7,989 rating pairs at 753 locations along 27 routes; the explanations were coded into streetscape features. Ratings and explanations per location are open on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.7712810).

Differences from the original study: (1) Google Street View images at 124 of the authors' 753 locations instead of the original images, which are not released; (2) locations are shown in random order instead of as a walk along a route; (3) the item wording and end labels are written from the abstract and dataset (5-point safety and attractiveness), not copied from the tool; (4) explanations are asked once at the end instead of after every location.
author: Milias, Sharifi Noorian, Bozzon & Psyllidis
